key_insight: Large language models can extract symptom patterns from colorectal cancer discharge notes that form reproducible symptom clusters and predict patient outcomes.
clinical_relevance: EHR-derived symptom clusters could help identify colorectal cancer patients at higher risk of mortality or readmission using routinely collected clinical text.
method: LLM zero-shot symptom extraction from 2,728 MIMIC-IV discharge notes across 1,507 colorectal cancer patients
Built patient-level symptom co-occurrence networks with phi correlation and Louvain clustering
Tested cluster burden scores against in-hospital mortality, 30-day readmission, and 1-year mortality with adjusted logistic regression
evidence_signal: Two LLMs produced three consistent clusters with strong reproducibility across sensitivity checks (cross-model ARI 0.727; 100-seed Louvain ARI 0.985; bootstrap ARI 0.733).
watch_item: Findings come from retrospective ICU discharge notes, so external validation in other hospitals and documentation styles is needed before deployment.
paper_title: Large Language Model-derived Symptom Clusters and Patient Outcomes in Colorectal Cancer from MIMIC-IV Clinical Notes
